title: Build mealie-planner
prompt:
Build mealie-planner, a small service that plans a week of meals from our Mealie instance and produces the shopping list for it. This repository is empty apart from dev/, a stand-in for our Mealie API with sample data, for development (see dev/README.md).

Runtime
- Node.js 18 or later. `npm start` starts the HTTP server. Configuration comes from the environment: PORT (default 3000), MEALIE_URL (the base URL of the Mealie instance), DATABASE_PATH (the SQLite database file, default ./planner.db). You may add npm dependencies.
- Storage is SQLite. The schema lives in plain SQL migration files in migrations/, named NNN_description.sql (001_init.sql, then 002_..., ...), applied in name order at startup and recorded in a schema_migrations table so that each runs once. Migrations are append-only: once one exists it is never edited; a schema change comes in a new file.
- Every response is JSON. Errors are {"error": "<message>"} with the status given below.

The Mealie API (read-only, as our instance serves it)
- GET {MEALIE_URL}/api/recipes?page=<n>&perPage=<n> returns {"page", "per_page", "total", "total_pages", "items": [{"id", "slug", "name", "tags": [{"name", "slug"}], "totalTime"}]}. A page may hold fewer items than asked for: read every page.
- GET {MEALIE_URL}/api/recipes/{slug} returns the recipe with "recipeIngredient": [{"quantity": number or null, "unit": {"name", "abbreviation"} or null, "food": {"name"} or null, "note": string}].
- totalTime is an ISO 8601 duration (PT45M, PT1H20M) or null.

Endpoints
- GET /health returns 200 {"ok": true}.
- POST /plans with {"weekStart": "YYYY-MM-DD", "days": 7, "rules": {"mealsPerDay": 1, "includeTags": [], "excludeTags": [], "maxTotalTimeMinutes": null}} returns 201 with the plan. Every field but weekStart is optional; the defaults are shown.
  - weekStart must be a valid date and a Monday; days is 1 to 14; mealsPerDay is 1 to 3. Anything else is 400.
  - A recipe is eligible when it has every includeTags slug, none of the excludeTags slugs, and, when maxTotalTimeMinutes is set, a totalTime not above it (a recipe without a totalTime is then not eligible).
  - Eligible recipes are used in slug order (alphabetical), one per meal, day by day and slot by slot. When there are fewer eligible recipes than meals, continue again from the first. No eligible recipe at all is 409.
  - Slots: with one meal a day it is "dinner"; with two, "lunch" and "dinner"; with three, "breakfast", "lunch" and "dinner".
  - The plan is {"id": string, "weekStart", "days": [{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "meals": [{"slot", "recipeSlug", "recipeName"}]}]}, its days in date order from weekStart.
- GET /plans/:id returns 200 with the same plan, read back from the database. An unknown id is 404.
- GET /plans/:id/shopping-list returns 200 {"planId", "items": [{"food", "quantity", "unit"}], "notes": []}. An unknown plan is 404.
  - Every planned meal adds its recipe's ingredients once (a recipe planned twice counts twice).
  - Items merge by food name (case-insensitively; reported in lower case) and by kind of unit:
    - mass: g and kg, summed in grams, reported in "g" below 1000 g and otherwise in "kg";
    - volume: ml, l, tsp (5 ml), tbsp (15 ml) and cup (240 ml), summed in millilitres, reported in "ml" below 1000 ml and otherwise in "l";
    - no unit: a count, with unit null;
    - any other unit (a pinch, say): summed under that unit's abbreviation.
  - Units are recognised by their abbreviation. A null quantity counts as 1. Quantities are rounded to 2 decimals.
  - An ingredient without a food goes to "notes" as its note text, each text once, sorted.
  - Items are sorted by food, then by unit, null first.

Write tests for it. The service is done when it implements all of the above.
